intro: The last array position may be padding. Summarize a variable-length sequence using the state at its last observed token.
task: Gather one hidden vector per example using valid lengths, returning zeros for empty sequences.
requirements: hidden is batch-by-time-by-features. lengths has one integer per example in 0..time.
Return a batch-by-features array: row b is hidden[b,lengths[b]-1] for a positive length and all zeros for length zero. Do not use negative indexing for empty rows.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Different lengths
examples.output:
[[1.0, 2.0], [7.0, 8.0]]
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Empty sequence
examples.output:
[[0.0, 0.0]]
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: One timestep
examples.output:
[[2.0], [0.0]]
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Convert a positive length to its last index by subtracting one.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Initialize zero rows and gather only examples whose length is positive.

explanation: Length-aware selection prevents padded states from replacing meaningful sequence summaries. It also supports a batch where some examples are empty without inventing a last token.
The gathered state is whatever representation the model supplied at that position. Whether it summarizes the whole prefix depends on the network architecture, not on this indexing operation.
